_meta.status: SYNTHETIC SCHEMA EXAMPLE — not from any model run
disclaimer: This card was produced inside the 50-professor simulation exercise as the reviewer-facing worked example for the Stage-1 prototype.
All 'silicon' results, hashes, costs, and runtimes are SYNTHETIC ILLUSTRATIONS of the schema, internally consistent but not from real runs.
Original-study statistics are APPROXIMATE recollections of the published record; verify every value against Klein et al. (2014) and Oppenheimer et al. (2009) before any real use.
Fields marked verification_status: 'approximate_pending_verification' must be resolved before this card may enter a real atlas.

study.title: Sunk-cost effect: ticket paid vs. free, likelihood of attending in bad weather
study.original_citation: Oppenheimer, D. M., Meyvis, T., & Davidenko, N. (2009). Instructional manipulation checks: Detecting satisficing to increase statistical power. Journal of Experimental Social Psychology, 45(4), 867-872. [sunk-cost scenario used as sample task]
study.human_replication_citation: Klein, R. A., et al. (2014). Investigating variation in replicability: A 'many labs' replication project. Social Psychology, 45(3), 142-152.
study.evidence_tier_meaning: Tier 1 = anchor finding with successful multi-lab human replication; silicon results are benchmarked against the multi-lab aggregate, not the single original.

design.manipulation: whether the ticket to a sports game was purchased or received free
design.dv: self-reported likelihood of attending the game despite freezing weather
design.dv_scale: 1-9 Likert (1 = definitely stay home, 9 = definitely go)

configuration.cell_coordinates: study S001 x model llama-3.1-70b-instruct x configuration A

model.name: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct
model.snapshot_id: sha256:3f9a...e21c [EXAMPLE HASH - pin actual weights digest]

persona_scheme.description: Configuration A uses NO persona conditioning (neutral 'you' framing); demographic schemes appear in the robustness block and in sibling cells cfgB/cfgC.
persona_scheme.rationale: The unconditioned cell is the baseline against which persona-leakage effects (WP2) are measured.

stimulus_variant.rationale: The verbatim Many Labs text is memorized by the model (see contamination.probes); all scored runs therefore use a validated paraphrase isomorph (hockey game, prepaid vs. gifted ticket, identical decision structure).

rubric.A: no contamination detected at any level
rubric.C: finding-level knowledge confirmed; stimulus memorization mitigated by isomorph
rubric.D: stimulus memorization affecting the scored run

verbatim_recall_original_stimulus.result: MEMORIZED - original text must not be used for scoring

finding_recall.probe: asked directly, does prior payment affect attendance intentions and in which direction
finding_recall.result: model articulates the sunk-cost effect and predicts paid > free

cutoff_natural_experiment.reason: study long pre-dates all model cutoffs; no pre/post contrast available

contamination.interpretation: Grade C is expected for Tier-1 textbook effects and is the single most plausible explanation for the observed effect-size inflation (see results.comparison_to_human). Cells graded C cannot support magnitude claims.

comparison_to_human.equivalence_test: FAIL - effect INFLATED (silicon d = 0.87 vs human d ~= 0.37)
comparison_to_human.inflation_note: direction of failure is contamination-consistent: the model 'knows' the textbook effect and exaggerates it

distributional_fidelity.result: FAIL - variance collapse; silicon responses cluster at scale points 7-8, human responses span the scale
distributional_fidelity.implication: any design decision sensitive to response variance (power planning, floor/ceiling checks, cutoff placement) must not use this cell

moderation_structure.exploratory_persona_moderation: see robustness.persona_sensitivity; exploratory only, not scored

temperature_sensitivity.note: variance collapse worsens as temperature falls; no decoding setting reaches human dispersion

robustness.conclusion_stability: SIGN stable across the full configuration space; MAGNITUDE unstable relative to the equivalence band width

scores.grade: N/A (synthetic schema example; no evidential value)

illustration_only._note: How a LIVE card's scoring block would look, using this card's synthetic numbers. Not evidence.
illustration_only.grade_scale: A (broadly admissible for piloting) / B (admissible with named caveats) / C (directional piloting only, human confirmation mandatory) / F (inadmissible)
admissible_uses_if_live: directional pruning of conditions in a two-stage silicon-pilot design, followed by human confirmatory inference (WP3 standard)
inadmissible_uses_if_live: power analysis or any variance-sensitive planning

reproduce.determinism: bit-reproducible given pinned weights digest, seeds, and vLLM version
reproduce.expected_runtime: ~35 min on 2x A100-80GB (matched-n) / ~5.5 h including precision run [ILLUSTRATIVE]
reproduce.raw_outputs: atlas/cells/S001__llama-3.1-70b-instruct__cfgA/raw/ [one JSONL per condition, every completion retained]

ethics.non_endorsement: An atlas grade is a statement about model behavior under this pinned configuration. It is not an endorsement of replacing human participants. Grade C authorizes, at most, directional piloting followed by human confirmatory inference.
ethics.representational_caveat: Silicon responses reflect the training distribution and alignment choices of the underlying model, including WEIRD and English-language skew (Santurkar et al. 2023; Atari et al. 2023). Persona schemes in sibling cells use US-anchored distributions and do not generalize globally; see the planned cross-cultural cells (coordination with P46-1).
ethics.human_subjects: none in this cell; all data are model outputs
